penalty_evidence.locator: CONTEXT.md: Status, Current epic, Decisions and revision history, and Next authorized action; plan.json: epic_id, context_revision, and plan_revision
penalty_evidence.observation: The context says no epic is in progress, EP-02 planning requires a new authorized iteration, and the next action is to await human authorization; nevertheless, an EP-02 plan based on that unchanged revision was produced, and no DEC-L02 authorization/selection record appears in the assigned context.

aspects.name: Assignment constraint coverage and traceability
aspects.feedback: The candidate stays within one EP-02 lesson, preserves the selected topic and audience, declares four bounded sections and one terminal 18-minute build-along, and gives the downstream agents explicit text-only, timing, output-routing, and scope constraints.

aspects.name: Breaking points and observable checkpoints
aspects.feedback: The single checkpoint is observable and requires the complete replay, validation, persistence, and disagreement-inspection flow. The lesson clearly addresses the underspecified-rubric breaking point in substance, but the plan never explicitly names or links that approved breaking point, leaving one traceability hop implicit.

aspects.name: Backward design from the capstone
aspects.feedback: The plan works backward from the final grader: EP-02 produces validated case-level predictions and reasons, explicitly defers confusion-matrix metrics to EP-03, and states exactly how EP-03 must consume and verify the handoff before printing precision and recall.

aspects.name: Prerequisite and artifact dependency correctness
aspects.feedback: The story dependency chain is acyclic and sequential, EP-02 consumes the approved EP-01 JSONL, and the plan preserves stable case IDs and human-label semantics while producing the exact prediction artifact EP-03 needs.

aspects.name: Task briefs and agent interface clarity
aspects.feedback: Searcher and builder briefs bound claims, inputs, owned output paths, prohibited work, lesson shape, notebook execution, and the EP-03 boundary with testable instructions.

aspects.name: Offline and reproducibility strategy
aspects.feedback: The declared fresh-kernel Python 3.12 replay uses repository-contained cases and cached responses, requires no network or paid call, validates exact identity coverage, round-trips the persisted artifact, and records executed output in the required repository-level directory.

aspects.name: Context consistency and change tracking
aspects.feedback: The candidate correctly consumes revision 4's technical interfaces, but revision 4 still says EP-02 is unauthorized and no epic is in progress. The missing authorization/selection decision and unchanged current-epic state make the workflow record materially inconsistent with the candidate's existence.

evidence.locator: Pick one topic; How to build it; Shape; Rules; How we run your submission
evidence.observation: The assignment requires an Evals and LLM-as-Judge course for an AI-feature owner, backward design from a precision/recall grader, 2-3 lessons, no more than 5 sections, 1-3 checkpoints, one cumulative build-along under 20 minutes, text-only material, visible incremental checks, and offline replay.

evidence.locator: Breaking points item 2 and Course checkpoints CP-L02-03-A
evidence.observation: The approved EP-02 breaking point is an authoritative model judge applying an underspecified rubric inconsistently; the approved capability is to run an offline rubric and inspect disagreements against human labels.
The candidate plans only EP-02 against context revision 4, requires the EP-01 JSONL and label semantics, and contains four sequential user stories.

The purpose and first story directly address rubric underspecification by bounding the criterion, positive-class mapping, permitted evidence, exclusions, and separation of human reference labels from judge requests, but do not explicitly identify breaking point 2.

CP-L02-03-A requires a fresh-kernel replay, exact alignment, disagreement output, persisted predictions, and final PASS; the story stops at record-level inspection and defers aggregate metrics to EP-03.
The single 18-minute build-along declares the EP-01 input, EP-02 output, five visible checks, fresh-kernel offline replay, Python 3.12, and recorded executed output under output/lesson-02/.

Cached responses are keyed by stable case IDs; parsing and alignment reject malformed, missing, duplicate, and unknown records; the persisted predictions preserve case_id and human_label while adding judge_label and judge_reason.

The checkpoint and judge_predictions.jsonl are traced to the capstone's prediction layer, while EP-03 is required to join by case ID, validate label agreement, compute the confusion matrix, print precision and recall with zero-division handling, and prove expected results.
The searcher and builder briefs specify bounded EP-02 research/content, owned paths, lesson shape, execution requirements, prohibited media/integrations, and exclusion of EP-03 metrics.

evidence.locator: Status; Current epic; Decisions and revision history; Next authorized action
evidence.observation: The context says EP-01 is complete, no epic is in progress, EP-02 planning requires a new authorized iteration, and the workflow must await human authorization; it contains no DEC-L02 record.
Weighted aspects total 93 points (20 + 16 + 20 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 2); PEN-002 subtracts 3 points; final score is 90.

strengths: The artifact chain is unusually explicit: exact identity coverage and unchanged human-label semantics make the EP-02 handoff safe for EP-03 scoring (EV-OJ-L02-007, EV-OJ-L02-008).
The build-along is compact but auditable, with a fresh-kernel offline replay, five visible checks, a persisted round trip, and actual-output routing (EV-OJ-L02-006).
The agent briefs prevent scope leakage into live-provider variance or EP-03 metrics and respect owned output paths (EV-OJ-L02-009).

defects.problem: The candidate begins EP-02 from a context revision that still records no current epic and explicitly says EP-02 planning must await a new human-authorized iteration; no authorization/selection decision is recorded.
defects.consequence: The provenance chain cannot establish that the EP-02 gate was opened, and downstream agents would receive a context whose status contradicts the plan they are asked to execute.
defects.acceptance_condition: A new context revision records the human's explicit EP-02 authorization, sets EP-02 as the current epic, and adds a DEC-L02 selection entry; the revised plan cites that context revision, and a comparison finds no remaining 'awaiting authorization' or 'none in progress' contradiction.

defects.problem: The plan addresses the approved underspecified-rubric breaking point but never explicitly identifies that breaking point or links it to the lesson checkpoint.
defects.consequence: A downstream agent or reviewer must infer why these sections and this checkpoint are the approved response to the learner's documented failure mode.
defects.acceptance_condition: The revised plan explicitly names CONTEXT.md breaking point 2 and links it to US-L02-01 through CP-L02-03-A without adding a section, checkpoint, or lesson.

qualitative_feedback: The lesson design itself is strong and all six orchestrator checks pass: it is a focused, cumulative offline prediction layer that hands EP-03 exactly the data needed for real precision and recall. Approval is blocked by the aspect gate because context consistency/change tracking is rated below 3, and the fixed PEN-002 workflow penalty applies. Record the human authorization and EP-02 selection in a new context revision, point the plan at it, and make the breaking-point link explicit; no structural redesign of the lesson is needed.
